Mas1e 1:14.en: Shout for joy to God our strength, shout for joy to the God of Jacob
Mas1e 1:14.notes: The transcription contains damage and uncertainty, particularly with the final word 'Jacob' (י ]ע##ק##ב##). The phrase 'shout for joy to God' is supported by repeated evidence, while 'the God of Jacob' is a common biblical expression.

Mas1e 1:15.en: Lift strength and give tambourine, cither, pleasant with harp.
Mas1e 1:15.notes: The transcription is partially damaged and reconstructed. The particle 'with' (ע##ם##) and the noun 'harp' (נ ]ב##ל##) are uncertain. The translation follows the visible morphology and lexical glosses, preserving the imperative structure and musical context.

Mas1e 1:16.en: Blow the horn in the month, at the full moon, to the day of the festival
Mas1e 1:16.notes: The phrase 'to the day of the festival' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The final word is uncertain due to damage in the source text.

Mas1e 1:17.en: For a decree to Israel, he is justice to the God of Jacob
Mas1e 1:17.notes: The phrase 'a decree to Israel' is supported by repeated evidence. 'He is justice' reflects the visible morphology and lexical glosses. 'To the God of Jacob' is a high-confidence contextual rendering, though the transcription of 'God' is uncertain.

Mas1e 1:18.en: A reminder in Joseph, he placed in going out upon the land of Egypt
Mas1e 1:18.notes: The phrase 'the land of Egypt' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The verb 'he placed' is reconstructed from the visible morphology. Uncertainty in the transcription is noted for 'א ]ר#ץ' and 'מצר##י#?ם##'.

Mas1e 1:19.en: My lip not I knew I hear from burden shoulder
Mas1e 1:19.notes: Uncertain reconstruction of 'lip' and 'burden'; contextual rendering of 'not I knew I hear' is ambiguous and retained as literal translation.

Mas1e 1:20.en: From the palm of the cooking pot they passed on in distress you called and I drew off
Mas1e 1:20.notes: Reconstructed and uncertain elements include the transcription and morphology of 'palm' (position 1), 'you called' (position 8), and 'I drew off' (position 10). The phrase 'David he passed on' is supported by repeated evidence but not directly reflected in the translation due to lack of direct licensing in the source tokens.

Mas1e 1:21.en: I will be humbled in the hiding place of thunder I will examine at the waters of Meribah sela
Mas1e 1:21.notes: The phrase 'at the waters of Meribah' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The verb 'examine' is uncertain due to damage in the source text.

Mas1e 1:22.en: Hear, O people, and I will again warn in Israel: if you hear the sound
Mas1e 1:22.notes: Uncertainty in the transcription affects the translation of 'Israel' and 'sound'. The phrase 'again in Israel' is supported by repeated evidence, but 'sound' has lower confidence.

Mas1e 1:23.en: It will not be in a strange god, and you must not bow down to a god of foreignness.
Mas1e 1:23.notes: The phrase 'you must bow down to a god of foreignness' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The phrase 'a strange god' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The translation conservatively follows the visible morphology and lexical glosses, preserving the uncertainty in the notes.

Mas1e 1:24.en: I am Yahweh your God who brought you up from the land of Egypt
Mas1e 1:24.notes: The phrase 'who brought you up' is uncertain due to damage in the source text. The phrase 'from the land of Egypt' is supported by repeated phrase evidence.

Mas1e 1:25.en: Widen my mouth and I will fill it and not hear my people's sound
Mas1e 1:25.notes: The phrase 'it has opened wide mouth' is a repeated phrase with moderate support, but it does not fit the context. The translation follows the visible morphology and lexical glosses instead. The final word 'sound' is a context-free gloss for 'קֹול', which is suffixed with 'י' indicating possession.

Mas1e 1:26.en: And Israel not he was willing to and I sent in the stubbornness their own heart
Mas1e 1:26.notes: The phrase 'not he was willing to' is a high-confidence contextual rendering. 'The stubbornness their own heart' is a repeated phrase with moderate support. The translation preserves all recoverable words and their order, with uncertainty in the reconstruction of the verb 'send' and its subject.

Mas1e 1:27.en: They will go in their counsels if only my people hear
Mas1e 1:27.notes: The phrase 'people they heard' is a repeated pattern, but 'my people hear' is more contextually appropriate. The verb 'walk' is translated as 'go' for natural English flow. The particle 'לו' is rendered as 'if only' to convey its conditional sense.

Mas1e 1:28.en: Israel in ways they walk as little their enemies I will humble
Mas1e 1:28.notes: Uncertainty in the transcription and reconstruction of 'א#ויבי׳הם' (enemies) noted.

Mas1e 1:29.en: And upon their adversaries I will turn my hand. He hates Yahweh, they cringed to him.
Mas1e 1:29.notes: The translation follows the visible morphology and phrase evidence. 'I will turn my hand' is supported by repeated phrase evidence (positions 4-5). 'He hates Yahweh' is supported by phrase evidence (positions 7-8). 'They cringed to him' is supported by phrase evidence (positions 9-10). No uncertainty or lacunae are present in the source.

Mas1e 2:1.en: And it will be their time to eternity. And he will feed him from the best of the wheat.
Mas1e 2:1.notes: The phrase 'best of the wheat' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The verb 'feed' is reconstructed from damaged text, and the preposition 'from' is uncertain.

Mas1e 2:2.en: And from the rock, honey, I am sated
Mas1e 2:2.notes: Uncertainty in the transcription and morphology of 'דב ]ש##' and 'א#שביע׳ך' may affect the translation.

Mas1e 2:3.notes: The transcription is partially damaged, with uncertainty in the first word. The phrase 'a psalm of Asaph' is supported by repeated evidence and matches the recoverable lexical items.

Mas1e 2:4.en: God stands in the congregation to God in the midst gods judge
Mas1e 2:4.notes: The phrase 'congregation to' and 'God [is] a judge' are supported by repeated phrase evidence. The sequence 'perhaps in midst' is less certain due to lower pattern support. The final verb 'judge' is in the imperfect tense, suggesting ongoing or habitual action.

Mas1e 2:5.en: Until when will you judge injustice and lift up the faces of the guilty sela
Mas1e 2:5.notes: The phrase 'wicked prince' is a repeated pattern but not directly supported here. 'Judges over' is a possible rendering of 'judge injustice' but less direct. 'Sela' is a musical notation, its meaning is unclear.

Mas1e 2:6.en: Judge the poor and the orphan, and be poor, and be just
Mas1e 2:6.notes: The transcription contains a reconstructed term ('הצדי[ קו ]') and a punctuation mark (׃) that cannot be translated independently. The term 'דל' is translated as 'poor' based on its morphology and lexical gloss, despite the alternative gloss 'door'. The term 'רש' is translated as 'be poor' based on its morphology and lexical gloss.

Mas1e 2:7.en: Escape, poor and needy, from the hand of the wicked, deliver!
Mas1e 2:7.notes: The phrase 'from the hand of the wicked' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The imperative verbs 'escape' and 'deliver' are translated directly from the visible morphology. The adjectives 'poor' and 'needy' are translated from the supplied context-free glosses, with 'needy' preferred over 'poor' for the second instance to avoid repetition.

Mas1e 2:8.en: They did not know and they did not understand in darkness they walk about
Mas1e 2:8.notes: The particle 'in' is uncertain due to damage. The translation preserves the visible morphology and lexical items, with no additional subjects or connectors introduced.

Mas1e 2:9.en: The whole foundations of the earth totter. I said, 'Gods, you are.'

Mas1e 2:10.en: And sons of the Most High, all of you, surely as humankind, you will die
Mas1e 2:10.notes: The phrase 'most high every' is supported by repeated evidence for positions 3-4. The phrase 'of humankind surely (die)' is supported by repeated evidence for positions 8-9.

Mas1e 2:11.en: And as one of the chiefs, fall! Arise, God, judge the earth.
Mas1e 2:11.notes: Uncertain transcription in positions 1 and 2. Phrase evidence supports 'one of the chiefs' and 'judge the earth'. 'Arise, God' is a possible interpretation of positions 8 and 9, but the pattern support is not dominant.

Mas1e 2:12.en: For you will take possession in all the nations.
Mas1e 2:12.notes: The verb 'תנ?ח##ל' is uncertain due to damage, but the context and morphology suggest 'take possession'. The phrase 'בכל הגוים' is supported by repeated phrase evidence as 'in all the nations'.

Mas1e 2:14.en: A song, a psalm of Asaph. Gods, not rest to you.
Mas1e 2:14.notes: The phrase 'a song, a psalm of Asaph' follows repeated phrase evidence. 'Gods' is plural per visible morphology. 'Not rest to you' follows repeated phrase evidence, with 'you' implied by the suffix on 'ל׳ך'.

Mas1e 2:15.en: Do not plough, and do not be at peace, God. Behold, your enemies make noise.
Mas1e 2:15.notes: The transcription contains significant damage, particularly in the latter half of the line. The phrase 'show quietness do not' is a repeated pattern with moderate support, influencing the translation of 'do not be at peace.' The final verb is highly uncertain due to extensive damage, but 'make noise' is retained as the most defensible gloss. Uncertainty is noted for several words, including the conjunction and the suffixed form.

Mas1e 2:16.en: And your haters will lift up the head upon your people they heap up confidential talk
Mas1e 2:16.notes: Uncertain elements include the form of 'haters' (position 2), the verb 'lift' (position 3), the meaning of 'head' (position 4), the preposition 'upon' (position 6), and the noun 'people' (position 7). The final word 'confidential talk' (position 9) is also uncertain. One word is reconstructed (position 8).

Mas1e 2:17.en: And they advised upon the hidden ones. They said, 'Go and hide them from the people.'
Mas1e 2:17.notes: The translation includes reconstructed and uncertain elements. The phrase 'he said go' is supported by repeated evidence, but the context suggests a plural subject. The verb 'hide' in the second clause is reconstructed and uncertain. The preposition 'from' is uncertain due to damage.

Mas1e 2:18.en: And the name of Israel will not be remembered still. That they advised heart together.
Mas1e 2:18.notes: The phrase 'the name of Israel' is supported by repeated evidence. The verb 'will not be remembered' is a conservative rendering of the nifal imperfect. 'Advised heart together' preserves the visible morphology and lexical items, with 'together' reconstructed from 'יח[ דו ]'.

Mas1e 2:19.en: Upon you a covenant they will cut. Gods, Edom and Ishmaelites.
Mas1e 2:19.notes: The phrase 'Upon you a covenant they will cut' reflects the uncertain reconstruction of 'עלי#?׳ך##בריתיכרתו'. 'Gods' translates 'אל#הי' with uncertainty. 'Ishmaelites' is a reconstructed form from 'ישמעאל##[ י ]ם##'.

Mas1e 2:20.en: Moab? and Hagrite, Gebal, Ammon and Amalek
Mas1e 2:20.notes: The first word is uncertain due to damage, indicated by a question mark in the transcription.

Mas1e 2:21.en: Philistia with dwellers in pebble even Asshur was accompanied with them
Mas1e 2:21.notes: The phrase 'dwellers in pebble' reflects a repeated phrase evidence for positions 3-4, though its meaning is unclear. The final 'with them' is a suffix on a damaged word, but the referent is uncertain.

Mas1e 2:22.en: It will be offspring to the descendants of Lot sela do to them as Midian as Sisera
Mas1e 2:22.notes: The phrase 'it will be offspring' is a high-confidence rendering of the first two words. 'To the descendants of Lot' is a repeated phrase with strong support. The sequence 'do to them' is a common construction, though less strongly supported here. The final three words are proper nouns or place names, translated directly.

Mas1e 2:23.en: As Jabin in the wadi of Kishon they were destroyed in Dor
Mas1e 2:23.notes: Uncertain characters in 'Kishon' and 'Dor' are omitted from the translation. The phrase 'the wadi of Kishon' is supported by repeated evidence.

Mas1e 2:24.en: They were dung to the soil. Put his willing ones as a raven and as a wolf.
Mas1e 2:24.notes: The translation follows the visible transcription and morphology. The verb 'היו' is rendered as 'They were' based on its perfect tense and third-person plural form. 'דמן' is translated as 'dung' and 'אדמה' as 'soil' per their lexical glosses. The particle 'ל' is translated as 'to'. The imperative 'שית׳מו' is rendered as 'Put' with 'his willing ones' reflecting the suffixed form 'נדיבי׳מו'. The particles 'כ' are translated as 'as'. 'ערב' and 'זאב' are rendered as 'raven' and 'wolf' respectively, with the conjunction 'ו' translated as 'and'.

Mas1e 2:25.en: And as a sacrifice, as Zalmunna, all their libation, which they said, 'We will take possession to'
Mas1e 2:25.notes: Uncertain reconstruction of 'Zalmunna' and 'whole'; 'libation' or 'leader' is contextually ambiguous; 'take possession to' is a paraphrased rendering of a repeated phrase with limited support.

Mas1e 2:26.en: The pastures of God, God will put as a wheel
Mas1e 2:26.notes: The transcription contains a damaged final segment 'כגלגל' which is translated as 'as a wheel' based on the visible form and lexical gloss. The object marker 'את' is omitted from the translation as it does not contribute to the propositional content. The repetition of 'אלהים' is preserved in the translation.

Mas1e 2:27.en: Like stubble before a wind, like a fire burning wood

Mas1e 2:28.en: And as a flame devours the mountains, so you will pursue them in a storm.
Mas1e 2:28.notes: The transcription contains an uncertain word at position 5 (ה#רים), which may affect the translation. The phrase 'a flame it has set ablaze' is a repeated phrase evidence for positions 3 and 4, but it was not used as it does not fit the context. The translation follows the visible morphology and lexical glosses, with the exception of the uncertain word.

Mas1e 2:29.en: And in your storm you will disturb them. Fill their faces with dishonour.
Mas1e 2:29.notes: The phrase 'Fill their faces' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The translation preserves the visible morphology and lexical items, with no uncertainty or reconstruction.

Mas1e 3:1.en: And they will seek the name of Yahweh. And they will be ashamed and disturbed until the end.
Mas1e 3:1.notes: The phrase 'the name of Yahweh' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The final word 'until the end' is a conservative translation of the repeated lexical item 'until' (עד), with the second instance likely indicating a temporal conclusion.

Mas1e 3:2.en: And they dig and perish and know that your name YHWH to alone
Mas1e 3:2.notes: Uncertain reconstruction of 'dig' (position 2). Uncertain transcription at position 1. Phrase evidence supports 'the name of Yahweh' but visible morphology shows 'your name YHWH'.

Mas1e 3:3.en: Most high upon all the earth
Mas1e 3:3.notes: The phrase 'most high above all' is supported by repeated evidence, though 'above' is reconstructed. 'All the earth' is a high-confidence phrase.

Mas1e 3:5.en: To the choirmaster upon the Gathite to the sons of Korah a psalm
Mas1e 3:5.notes: The term 'גתית' (Gathite) lacks a trusted gloss; 'upon' is reconstructed. Phrase evidence strongly supports 'to the sons of Korah a psalm' as a repeated pattern.

Mas1e 3:6.en: What beloved dwelling-places of Yahweh of hosts
Mas1e 3:6.notes: Reconstructed and uncertain elements present in the source. The phrase 'dwelling-places' is a reconstruction of the damaged word. 'Yahweh of hosts' is a high-confidence contextual rendering of the phrase 'יהוה צבאות'.

Mas1e 3:7.en: She longed and even was complete my soul to the courts of YHWH
Mas1e 3:7.notes: Reconstructed text in position 4. The transcription is partially damaged, and the translation reflects the recoverable words in order.

Mas1e 3:8.en: Heart and flesh, they cry out to the living God
Mas1e 3:8.notes: The phrase 'God living' is supported by repeated evidence. The verb 'cry out' is reconstructed from 'יר[ ננו'.

Mas1e 3:9.en: Also a bird found the house and a swallow a nest to her
Mas1e 3:9.notes: Reconstructed text and uncertainty in the verb 'found' noted. Phrase evidence supports 'was] found the house' but is not directly applied due to visible morphology constraints.

Mas1e 3:10.en: which put the young ones of your altars
Mas1e 3:10.notes: Reconstructed text in position 3. The phrase 'young ones of your altars' is uncertain due to the fragmentary nature of the source.

Mas1e 3:11.en: YHWH of hosts, Melech of gods, blessed are the inhabitants of your house
Mas1e 3:11.notes: The transcription contains a reconstructed word and an unknown punctuation mark. The phrase 'YHWH of hosts' is supported by high-confidence evidence. 'Melech of gods' is a conservative rendering of the visible morphology. 'Blessed are the inhabitants of your house' follows the supplied glosses and repeated phrase evidence.

Mas1e 3:12.en: Still they will praise you, sela. Blessed is the man with power in you
Mas1e 3:12.notes: The transcription is partially damaged, and the particle 'ס#[ לה' is reconstructed and uncertain. The phrase 'ל׳ו ב׳ך' is translated based on repeated phrase evidence, but its exact meaning in this context is unclear.

Mas1e 3:13.en: Highways in their heart, they passed in the valley of the baka-shrub
Mas1e 3:13.notes: The transcription contains a damaged word (מ#סלות) and an uncertain gloss for the final noun (בכא). The translation preserves the visible morphology and lexical items, but the exact sense of 'בכא' remains unclear.

Mas1e 3:14.en: A well they put, even blessings he will cover, a teacher
Mas1e 3:14.notes: The translation follows the visible morphology and lexical glosses. The final word 'מורה' is translated as 'teacher' based on its lexical gloss. The sentence structure is fragmented, and no additional connectors or subjects are added. The transcription ends with a punctuation mark (׃) which is not translated.

Mas1e 3:15.en: They will walk from strength to strength, he will see to God in Zion
Mas1e 3:15.notes: The phrase 'O God in Zion' is supported by repeated phrase evidence, but the translation retains the visible morphology and word order. The reconstruction of 'ח[ יל' is noted but not bracketed in the translation.

Mas1e 3:16.en: Yahweh God of hosts hear prayer
Mas1e 3:16.notes: Reconstructed text in position 3. Uncertain readings in positions 1 and 2.

Mas1e 3:17.en: Listen, the God of Jacob Selah, his shield saw God
Mas1e 3:17.notes: The transcription is partially damaged and reconstructed. The term 'סלה' is transliterated as 'Selah' due to its uncertain meaning. The phrase 'מגנ׳נו ראה אלהים' is translated conservatively, preserving the ambiguity of the shield's agency.

Mas1e 3:18.en: And look at the face of your anointed, that good days in your courts
Mas1e 3:18.notes: The transcription is partially damaged and reconstructed. The verb 'look at' is reconstructed from 'ה##[ בט'. The phrase 'the face of your anointed' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The phrase 'good days in your courts' is also supported by repeated phrase evidence, though with lower confidence.

Mas1e 3:19.en: From a thousand I have examined to stand at the threshold in the house of God
Mas1e 3:19.notes: The phrase 'thousand chosen [man]' is supported by repeated evidence but not directly reflected in the visible text. The possessive 'my' or 'our' in 'house of God' is not recoverable from the transcription and is omitted. The infinitive construct 'to stand at the threshold' is translated as a purpose clause, a natural English construction.

Mas1e 3:20.en: From dwelling in the tent of the guilty, that the sun and shield of Yahweh God
Mas1e 3:20.notes: Reconstructed and uncertain elements include 'ד[ ו ]ר##' (circulate/dwell) and 'אה##[ לי' (tent). The phrase 'tent of the guilty' is supported by repeated evidence. 'Yahweh God' is a high-confidence rendering of 'יהוה אלהים'.

Mas1e 3:21.en: Grace and honor he will give YHWH, who does not withhold good from those walking in integrity.
Mas1e 3:21.notes: The phrase 'honor I will give' and 'withhold good' are supported by repeated phrase evidence. The reconstruction of 'YHWH' is based on the lemma and context.

Mas1e 3:22.en: Yahweh of hosts, blessed is the man who trusts in you
Mas1e 3:22.notes: The phrase 'Yahweh of hosts' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. 'Blessed is the man' is a conservative rendering of the visible morphology. 'Who trusts in you' is supported by phrase evidence and preserves the grammatical relationships.

Mas1e 3:24.en: To the choirmaster of the sons of Korah a psalm
Mas1e 3:24.notes: The phrase 'to the choirmaster of the sons of Korah a psalm' is supported by repeated phrase evidence and canonical patterns. The transcription includes a reconstructed word 'מזמ[ ור' (psalm) and an unknown punctuation mark '׃' which is omitted in the translation.

Mas1e 3:25.en: You desired, Yahweh, the land of their captivity, Jacob.
Mas1e 3:25.notes: The phrase 'the captivity of Jacob' is supported by repeated evidence. The verb 'return' is implied by the context but not directly recoverable from the visible text.

Mas1e 3:26.en: You lifted sin of your people, you covered all their sins. Sela.
Mas1e 3:26.notes: The phrase 'they were covered all' is a repeated pattern with moderate support, but it contradicts the visible morphology and person agreement. The translation follows the visible DSS transcription and morphology instead. The phrase 'all sins' is a repeated pattern with strong support and aligns with the visible morphology, so it is used. The phrase 'I lifted up eyes' is a repeated pattern but does not match the visible morphology or the context, so it is not used. The final translation preserves the grammatical person, number, and semantic relationships from the source text.

Mas1e 3:27.en: You gathered all your anger, you returned from the burning of your anger
Mas1e 3:27.notes: The phrase 'from the burning his anger' is a high-confidence contextual rendering of positions 5-7. The translation follows the visible morphology and lexical glosses, with 'burning' interpreted as a contextual sense for 'anger' based on repeated phrase evidence.

Mas1e 3:28.en: Let us return to the God of our help and stir up your grief with us
Mas1e 3:28.notes: The translation follows the visible morphology and lexical glosses. The phrase 'שוב׳נו אלהי' is rendered as 'Let us return to the God' based on the imperative form of 'שוב' and the plural suffix. 'ישע׳נו' is translated as 'our help' following the gloss and suffix. 'הפר' is rendered as 'stir up' based on the hifil stem and gloss. 'כעס׳ך' is translated as 'your grief' following the gloss and suffix. 'עמ׳נו' is rendered as 'with us' based on the gloss and suffix. The final mark is omitted as it has no recoverable gloss.

Mas1e 3:29.en: Will you be angry forever, drawing your nose to a generation and a generation?
Mas1e 3:29.notes: The phrase 'drawing your nose' is a literal translation of the visible morphology, though its meaning is uncertain. The repetition of 'generation' reflects the source text's repetition of 'דר'.
